en.html:
The bandits had set up base on a small mountain outside town.
Geologically speaking, it is an upheaval belonging to the rugged mountain system in the north. In practice it is too big to be called a hill and too small to be called a mountain, so "small mountain" it is. I see no better word.

In the old days this was, naturally, where the town's children played. They were cleared off completely, with warning shots and bare blades, and the reason was not that the bandits hated children. The bandits simply liked this mountain even more than the children did.

It was close enough to overawe the town, and getting in and out gave no trouble. If the bandits believed this mountain to be their Canaan, I could find no argument to refute them.
I would still refuse a god who makes promises of that quality.

山賊団は郊外の小山に拠点を敷いている。
　地形学的に見れば北の険しい山脈系に属する隆起だ
が、実質としては丘と呼ぶには大きく山岳と呼ぶには
小さい程度のもので、やはり小山と呼ぶほかにない。

　ここは過去、当然のように町の子供の遊び場だった。
　彼らが威嚇射撃と白刃の脅しで根こそぎ追い払われ
てしまったのは、子供たち以上に山賊団にとってこの
山が好物件だったからである。

山賊団がこの山を<ruby>約束の地<rt>カナーン</rt></ruby>だと信じていたとしても、
否定の論拠は見つかりそうになかった。
　そんなろくでもない約束をする神は御免だが。

She let out a pitying laugh on her breath and took one step. The smoothness and suppleness of it told me her level.

Strong.

Exactly as I had known from the start.

She was stronger than I am.

I had put the odds of that at better than even.

So I held her in contempt. On purpose.

If talking did not settle it, I would bring it down to a contest with the leader and finish it there. That was the plan, and its biggest problem was how to be sure of winning.

Nobody needs to argue the strength of Rokuhara's army. Its warriors—its dragoons—in particular have few equals anywhere in the world. That is exactly why GHQ accepted their surrender and gave them the governing rights over Yamato as the price.

This woman had served in that Rokuhara. And she had won near-perfect loyalty from her men, since she had lost her military standing and still kept them around her; that much could not be doubted.

When a warrior commands an infantry unit in the shogunate army, he is very often the head (or heir) of a middle-rank warrior house, and the soldiers are his clan and retainers. The tie of lord and servant is not of yesterday. It is traditional.

Even so, if that head were soft and useless, they would have dropped her the moment she lost her position, and nobody could blame them. Tradition may strengthen loyalty, but it holds up nothing by itself.

She was, first of all, a person of real strength, worthy of the name of Rokuhara warrior. That strength kept her men with her. In martial courage, she was not someone who would trail behind others.

My chance of winning a fair fight was thin.
To win, I had to make her careless.

A plain challenge would not do. When a warrior is challenged by an ordinary townsman, she will feel nine parts mockery, and one part caution.

And with that one part in place, no opening appears.
My chances would stay small.

So I held her in contempt.
I would show her a fool who looks down on her, thinking, she's only a woman after all.

If the act succeeded, her anger and her contempt would join. She would want not merely to win but to crush me.

Her swordwork would turn loose and coarse. And it would not be a killing stroke.

One blow that killed me would give her no chance to taste the humiliation. She would most likely go for an arm or a leg.

...If I could hold the whole situation in my palm to that extent, then even an opponent who outdid me in skill—

en.html:
Tonight, Hikaru was resting quietly. Her breathing sounded a little gentler too, though only by comparison.

Even so, there was not a hair's sign of recovery. The color of life drains on and on. Its speed rises and falls, and today it happened to lean toward slow. That Hikaru draws nearer to death each day is unchanged.

I had come back late, so I held off reporting to the senior house for tonight. I went straight home and told only my foster mother how things stood.

She was glad that I was safe, but she did not look pleased about the whole business at the bandit fort. It showed that she did not consider it the best resolution.

I felt the same. Otherwise I would have gone to the senior house at that hour, rudeness and all.

...I do think that was the only move I had.

I hardly needed to study the woman's face to see that acceptance was missing from it. Her belief that she would win a second round was far deeper than any sense that she had lost this one.

The bandits could not have accepted it either. Probably even less than their leader.

Still, it was a contest held under a clear agreement.

It was only a spoken promise, but that was not the problem. The promise had been exchanged in front of everyone, and the result was plain as day.

It was hard to imagine someone of warrior-house origin pretending not to see an established fact and carrying on regardless. The promise would be kept. It should be kept.

窺えた。

　そうでなければ、夜分に訪いを入れる非礼を犯して
でも本家に寄っていったろう。

　……あの手しか無かったとは、思うのだが。

　女首領の表情は詳細に観察するまでもなく、納得と
いう成分を欠いていた。
　負けたと思うよりも、もう一度やれば勝つとの思い
の方が遥かに深かったことは疑いない。

　おそらくは首領以上に。

　しかし、あれは明確な取り決めのもと行われた勝負
である。

　約束は環視の中で確かに取り交わされたし、決着も
明々白々だった。

　仮にも武家の出である者が、確かな事実に頬被りを
決め込むとは考えにくい。
　約束は守られるだろう――守られる筈だ。

The memory of the origin.

Mother taking Father.
Father taken by Mother.
Myself losing Father.

Again.
And again.

I go on dreaming the same dream.
In a world of darkness without end.

That is the only thing the one called Hikaru is allowed.

The dark will never let me go.
It orders me to rot here.

It orders me not to move.

Yes.
Hikaru must not move from here.

If I, who had Father taken away, were to move this life, it would be to bring Father back.

I who was robbed
move only to take back.

But that is not allowed.

—Father is Mother's. Mother is Father's.
For a child to take Father from Mother is strictly forbidden by the human path.

Hikaru is human.
I cannot turn my back on the human path.

If I follow the human path, I am not allowed to take Father back from Mother.

If I turn my back on the human path and try to take him anyway,
Father will not acknowledge Hikaru.

So Hikaru cannot move from the bottom of this dark.

I began as the one who was robbed. With no road open to take back what was taken, I have no way to be except to remain forever at the origin.

...So Hikaru is here.
Here for good.
